label: digit 3 fed back as input during copy phase (later positions)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, only when the input token is the digit 3 (the model own previous output being 3). It never fires on 3 in the original phase, at the delimiter, or on any other input token. Rate is near zero for recall_idx 1, low (~0.7%) at recall_idx 2 and ~3% (about 75-90% of qualifying 3-inputs) for recall_idx >= 3; restricting to recall_idx >= 3 gives dev F1 0.87 with 97% mass recall. Magnitude is largest when the 3 sits late in the copy and is the first of a run of repeated 3s (e.g. ...3 3 -> first 3 at ~1.0, second at ~0.3-0.6); early-position 3s (recall_idx 1-2) give weak activations. Remaining false positives are qualifying 3-inputs with no activation, with no clear pattern.

issues: Most claims hold. All activation mass is in the copy phase and in_tok==3 accounts for 100% of it. The feature never fires in the original or delimiter phases or on any other input token. Firing rate by recall_idx is 1:0.000, 2:0.007, >=3:~0.03 of all steps. Top examples show the first 3 of a run at ~0.9-1.0 of max and the following 3 at 0.26-0.68. Low-quartile examples are early-position 3s.

Test scores reproduce: P 0.820, R 0.935, F1 0.874, mass recall 0.968. Alternatives score lower: recall_idx>=2 gives F1 0.81, recall_idx>=4 gives 0.78, and the unrestricted in_tok==3 in copy phase gives 0.72.

The claim that the remaining false positives have 'no clear pattern' is wrong. Within the predicate, precision depends strongly on out_tok, the token after the 3 in the original sequence (the one about to be output). Precision by out_tok: v 0.999, c 0.99, 3 0.999, q 0.97, x 0.97, e 0.96, u 0.95, 1 0.95. Versus: 0 0.31, r 0.60, w 0.63, s 0.65, i 0.67, n 0.67, a 0.76. About 6 of the 27 next-token values account for roughly 40-45% of the ~10.4k test false positives.

Precision also rises steadily with position (recall_idx 3: 0.69, 4: 0.85, >=5: 0.88), so the recall_idx>=3 cutoff approximates a graded position effect rather than a sharp threshold. L<=5 gives precision 0.74 vs 0.84 for L>=8.

The next-token effect is graded, not an on/off gate. Excluding the low-precision next tokens lowers test F1 to 0.837, and adding recall_idx==2 for high-precision next tokens gives 0.835. So the original predicate is still the best binary rule; the problem is that the explanation misses this effect, not that the predicate is wrong.
The label 'later positions' is consistent with the predicate. It does not mention that the token after the 3 in the original sequence affects firing.
skeptic.revised_label: digit 3 fed back as input during copy phase (later positions); strength grows with position and depends on the token that follows the 3 in the original sequence (weak or absent when next is 0, r, w, s, i or n)
